title: Dataverse: build solutions with coding agents using the Dataverse plugin and Work IQ
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing statements and governance controls are supported by the record and Microsoft documentation. It correctly distinguishes optional plugin installation, Dataverse MCP controls, Work IQ participation and directly authenticated tools.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans natural-language coding-agent development of Dataverse solutions.
claims.quote: Build Dataverse solutions by using coding agents with natural language prompts.

claims.claim: In the recruiting-system example, the agent discovers the Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: Discovers your Dataverse environment and configures MCP.

claims.claim: The example agent configures MCP.
claims.quote: Discovers your Dataverse environment and configures MCP.

claims.claim: The example agent creates a solution using Power Platform CLI.
claims.quote: Creates the solution by using the Microsoft Power Platform CLI.

claims.claim: The example agent builds tables with lookups.
claims.quote: Builds five tables with choice columns, lookups, and a many-to-many relationship.

claims.claim: The example includes a many-to-many relationship.
claims.quote: Builds five tables with choice columns, lookups, and a many-to-many relationship.

claims.claim: The example agent generates and runs a Python script to bulk-load sample data.
claims.quote: Generates and runs a Python script to bulk-load realistic sample data.

claims.claim: The example agent queries across tables.
claims.quote: Queries across tables to answer your business question.

claims.claim: The plugin supports packaging and deploying solutions.
claims.quote: Package and deploy solutions | dv-solution

claims.claim: The plugin prerequisites require a Dataverse environment through Power Apps, Dynamics 365 or another applicable Power Platform plan.
claims.quote: A Dataverse environment available through Power Apps, Dynamics 365, or another applicable Power Platform plan.

claims.claim: The developer needs an account with access and privileges for the requested operations.
claims.quote: A user account with access to the environment and the privileges required for the operations you request.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT, Gemini CLI and Google Antigravity as supported agents.
claims.quote: A supported agent: GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT, Gemini CLI, or Google Antigravity.

claims.quote:
### GitHub Copilot

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP client applications require tenant administrator consent.
claims.quote: A tenant administrator grants consent to the MCP client application.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP clients require per-environment allowlisting.
claims.quote: An environment administrator allows the client application in each target environment.

claims.claim: The Dataverse SDK for Python and Power Platform CLI authenticate directly and are outside the MCP-specific controls.
claims.quote: Other tools used by the plugin, such as the Dataverse SDK for Python and Power Platform CLI, authenticate directly and aren't subject to these MCP-specific controls.

claims.claim: Directly authenticated plugin-tool requests still require Dataverse authorization.
claims.quote: Their requests still require Dataverse authorization.

claims.claim: Business skills require Work IQ enabled in the environment.
claims.quote: A Dataverse environment with Work IQ enabled by a Power Platform administrator.

claims.claim: Microsoft turns on Business Applications in Work IQ by default for qualifying new public production environments from September 30, 2026.
claims.quote: Starting September 30, 2026, Microsoft turns on these capabilities by default for all new environments that aren't listed as exceptions in this article.

claims.claim: Microsoft turns on Business Applications in Work IQ for qualifying existing environments from November 2026.
claims.quote: Starting in November 2026, Microsoft turns on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptions.

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to the Work IQ default enablement during public preview.
claims.quote: During public preview, customers can turn on Work IQ by using the corresponding setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to Work IQ default enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to Work IQ default enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: Dataverse table rows, including loaded sample rows, consume database capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse - Database capacity: Tracks structured data stored directly in Dataverse, including table rows, metadata, and relational data created by Power Apps, Power Automate, Dynamics 365 customer engagement apps

claims.claim: Work IQ search indexes use extra storage.
claims.quote: Some features use extra storage for search indexes. These features include semantic modeling and access to Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Preview plugin use does not remove underlying service charges.

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ participation is configured in Power Platform admin center at Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote:
Select Manage, and select the environment.
Select Settings > Product > Features.
Locate Work IQ.
Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: No API or automation equivalent for the environment Work IQ participation switch was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "environment" "Power Platform API" settings; "Work IQ" "Set-TenantSettings" "pac admin" "Power Platform API"; "Work IQ" "environment" "organization EntityType" enable. Read manage-participation and default-settings; no equivalent found.

claims.claim: The tenant control is in Microsoft 365 admin center at Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings.
In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.claim: No documented API or automation equivalent for the tenant business-applications availability control was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot" API PowerShell; "Work IQ" "tenant setting" "Graph" "beta". Opened default-settings and manage-ai-experience-access; no equivalent command or endpoint found.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP configuration is in Power Platform admin center at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol.
claims.quote:
Select Manage > Environments.
Select the Environment Name ... select Settings. Under Settings, select Product > Features. Scroll down to locate Dataverse Model Context Protocol

claims.claim: Allowed MCP client records are listed under Advanced Settings.

Select Advanced Settings.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP can be blocked in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > Tools.

claims.claim: No documented API equivalent for blocking the entire Work IQ MCP server was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "block" "Graph" API; "Work IQ MCP" "Block" "Graph API" availability. Opened manage-ai-experience-access and read migration rollback search results; no server-availability management endpoint found.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; controls[4].api; controls[4].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: No separate admin UI or API switch specifically governing coding-agent Dataverse plugin use is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "AI coding agents" "disable" "policy"; "Dataverse plugin" administrator disable switch price licensing. Opened agents-plugin/, coding-agents and security-governance; found identity permissions and MCP controls, not a separate coding-plugin switch.

claims.claim: The signed-in developer's Dataverse privileges govern the plugin's operations.
claims.quote: An agent can't exceed the permissions of the signed-in identity. If that identity lacks a required privilege, the operation fails.

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant cascade setting stops sharing between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse even when an app is configured to share.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, data isn't shared between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse, even if an app is configured to share data.

claims.claim: Service-principal authentication is available and the agent remains limited to that principal's permissions.
claims.quote: Service-principal authentication is available for unattended scenarios. Service-principal tokens are held in memory rather than persisted. The agent can't exceed the authenticated user's or service principal's permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft explicitly says Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic access.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP Block control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access.

claims.claim: The allowed-client REST call updates one allowed MCP client record.
claims.quote: An MCP client that is allowed to talk to MCP endpoint; Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients; Primary key: allowedmcpclientid

claims.claim: The allowed-client record update is not the server-wide Dataverse MCP setting.
claims.quote:
Admins can disable MCP for Dataverse by clearing the setting.
On the MCP client record, set Is Enabled to Yes.

claims.claim: Business skills can be shared through general access.
claims.quote: General access—Makes the skill available to everyone in the environment.

claims.claim: Business skills can be shared using Dataverse security roles.
claims.quote: Security role access—Provides access based on Dataverse security roles.

claims.claim: Business skills can be shared by direct access.
claims.quote: Direct access—Shares the skill with specific users or groups and lets you choose whether they can view or edit the skill.

claims.claim: Role-based skill access requires both Skill Sharing Role and the security role with which the skill is shared.
claims.quote: An administrator must assign users the Skill Sharing Role, either directly or through a team. Users must also have the security role that the skill is shared with.

claims.claim: The coding-agent plugin is user-opt-in, independently of Work IQ's default-enablement rollout.
claims.quote:
Install the plugin for your coding agent.
### GitHub Copilot
/plugin install dataverse@awesome-copilot

claims.claim: The documented costs combine service consumption with the coding agent's separate subscription or consumption charges, consistent with mixed licensing.
claims.quote:
Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences.
The coding agent's own subscription or consumption charges are separate.

claims.claim: A variable cost rating is consistent with the documented Copilot Credit meter.
claims.quote: The search_data tool uses usage-based Copilot Credit billing rather than a fixed charge per tool call.
